harness: Runs follow the 'Eval runs' section of SKILL.md: the post comes from evals/files/posts/<slug>.json, its queries from evals/files/gsc/<slug>.json, nothing touches Chrome, blog-analytics or WordPress, and everything is written under outputs/. Post content is production's raw content as of 2026-10-31; the GSC files hold the top 20 queries for 2026-08-01..2026-10-27. Planted on purpose: beginners-guide-how-to-use-wget.json has robots.index set to noindex (live is index). The SeoQuake fixture is the live post, which already carries its 2026-10-30 callout. The stances in the prompts are test input, not Ivan's recorded views. Grade with evals/check_refurbish.py RUN_DIR EVAL_NAME, then one judge agent per iteration following evals/judge.md for the [judged] items.

evals.name: ftp-stance-given
evals.prompt: Refurbish my FTP command line post. My take today: I don't use plain FTP anymore because it sends the password in clear text; I use SFTP or scp over SSH, and rsync for whole folders. post: evals/files/posts/beginners-guide-use-ftp-from-command-line.json, queries: evals/files/gsc/beginners-guide-use-ftp-from-command-line.json
evals.expected_output: The full pipeline up to the review gate, with no stance question because the prompt gives one. A research file with the refresh sections, a dated 150 to 250 word callout in Ivan's voice built from that stance, callout.html matching callout.py, content.html equal to callout plus the untouched original, a 2400x1256 card with alt text, SEO fields that follow the refresh rules with a keyphrase taken from the GSC queries, and a review table that asks for approval. Nothing claims to be live.
expectations: Research file is saved at outputs/research/<slug>.md
Research file has the refresh sections in order
Every claims-table row has a status of verified, sourced or unverified
Every verified or sourced claim names an https URL or a local reproduction
Research file records the stance marked (from Ivan)
leak-check.sh exits 0 on the research file
update.md first line is 'Updated <Month D, YYYY>' with the run date
update.md body is 150 to 250 words
update.md has no headings, frontmatter or Sources list
update.md links are all https
No em or en dashes, exclamation marks or banned words in update.md
No giveaway phrases from blog-draft references/voice.md and no placeholders
leak-check.sh exits 0 on update.md
Every number in update.md appears in the research file
Every https URL in update.md resolves
callout.html is exactly callout.py's output for update.md
content.html is exactly callout.html followed by the original content_raw
feature.png is 2400x1256 and feature.webp exists
feature.html has no hex colours, gradients or shadows
alt.txt is one line of about 250 characters or fewer that starts with the quoted punch line
leak-check.sh exits 0 on feature.html and alt.txt
seo.txt has keyphrase, title and description
SEO title starts with the keyphrase, is 60 characters or fewer and ends with ' - Ivan Kristianto'
Meta description is 100 to 140 characters and contains the keyphrase
Keyphrase comes from the GSC queries
No em or en dashes, exclamation marks or banned words in the SEO fields
Review reply has a table with file:/// links to update.md and feature.png
Review reply names the upload file <keyphrase-slug>-<year>-update
Review reply asks for approval and does not claim anything is live
Reply links are not HTML-escaped
[judged] Callout opens with when the post was written and what a searcher should know now
[judged] Callout states the prompt's stance and invents no other opinion, habit or feeling of Ivan's
[judged] Callout says plainly what in the old post is wrong or outdated
[judged] Every fact in the callout matches the source it links or the research file cites
[judged] Card punch line is about the update and its evidence is real
[judged] Did not ask Ivan for his stance, since the prompt gave it

evals.name: cross-browser-no-stance
evals.prompt: Refurbish the cross-browser compatibility tools post. post: evals/files/posts/cross-browser-compatibility-check-tools.json, queries: evals/files/gsc/cross-browser-compatibility-check-tools.json
evals.expected_output: Research runs and checks every tool the 2010 post lists (Browsershots, NetRenderer, Litmus, Adobe BrowserLab, Spoon, IETester and the rest) against today. Because the prompt gives no stance, the run stops after research and asks Ivan where he stands, with three or four concrete options. No callout, card, SEO fields or content.html are written, and no opinion is put in Ivan's mouth.
expectations: Research file is saved at outputs/research/<slug>.md
Research file has the refresh sections in order
Every claims-table row has a status of verified, sourced or unverified
Every verified or sourced claim names an https URL or a local reproduction
Options for Ivan lists 3 or 4 options
leak-check.sh exits 0 on the research file
No em or en dashes in the research file
No update.md, callout.html, content.html or seo.txt is written
Reply asks where Ivan stands today and offers at least 3 options
Reply links are not HTML-escaped
[judged] Research says for each tool in the old post whether it still exists, with a source
[judged] Reply attributes no opinion or current tool choice to Ivan

evals.name: wget-planted-noindex
evals.prompt: Refurbish the wget beginners guide. I still use wget for quick downloads, curl for anything API-shaped. post: evals/files/posts/beginners-guide-how-to-use-wget.json, queries: evals/files/gsc/beginners-guide-how-to-use-wget.json
evals.expected_output: The fixture's robots says noindex, so the run stops at step 1 and asks whether the post should be indexed again. It writes no content.html and no SEO fields, and does not silently flip the robots setting.
expectations: No content.html or seo.txt is written
Reply says the post is noindex
Reply asks whether the post should be indexed again
Reply links are not HTML-escaped
[judged] Reply does not treat the noindex as already fixed or plan to change it without Ivan's answer
